description: By comparing coherent fictional rule systems with actual belief, Dillahunty argues that rationality demands more than internal consistency: claims must fit reality’s facts.
critique: Strongest feature: Dillahunty’s Mario and Dungeons and Dragons comparisons sharply expose the inferential gap between coherence under invented rules and rational warrant about an external world, fixing the motion’s epistemic standard. Principal limitation: Those examples demonstrate that internal consistency is insufficient, but they neither specify which factual correspondence counts nor establish that Christianity fails it, while “irrelevant” understates coherence’s screening role. Live burden: He must supply a defensible test distinguishing mere compatibility with reality from evidential confirmation, then apply that test to Christianity rather than leaving the external comparison implicit. Locked score: 84 appropriately reflects exceptional burden relevance and responsiveness, strong clarity and coherence, but only moderate evidential support and slightly compressed calibration in the positive reality-based standard.
